floor_history.headline: Re-ran discarded s1 recon: applied inherited candidate.c to src/main.c, re-measured honest floor 38 (was claimed 37 pre-discard), banked explicit per-symbol OBJECT MODEL verdicts for both flagged SPLI

s1's recorded floor of 38 was false (8 undeclared-identifier implicit-int bugs); fixing declaration order drops the honest floor to 19; a u16-mask lever for the per-voice loop exit was tried and kille

frontier.hypothesis: Read the .greg/.sched dump content (not just cc1 stderr) for the floor-19 body's _SsVmInit region and pass-attribute the remaining ~19-insn residual before proposing further specific-register-seat levers.
frontier.mechanism: n/a -- diagnostic step, mandated by the PASS ATTRIBUTION contract before further guessing.

frontier.hypothesis: Explicitly hoist the shared 0xFF constant (currently written as the literal 0xFF at both the D_800F4E18 and D_800F4E2E store sites) into a single local variable set once before the per-voice loop and read twice inside it, matching target's single-materialization-in-$s1-before-the-loop shape.
frontier.mechanism: Named-intermediate / staged-value family (a fresh or loop-hoisted local reused across two same-value stores) -- if this closes bytes, it needs the family's prerequisites (no-new-park-categories.md) checked before banking; if it's simply what GCC 2.7.2 naturally does when the value is loop-invariant and used twice, no annotation is needed at all (ordinary C, Ruling 1 in ordinary-c-judge-decidable.md).
frontier.next_probe: Declare a local (e.g. `s16 ff = 0xFF;`) before the per-voice do-while, replace both literal 0xFF stores with reads of it, re-measure sandbox --disable all.

frontier.hypothesis: Target hoists the buf-array address ($a0 = sp+0x10) once before the per-voice loop rather than re-deriving it per func_8008B488 call; check whether this already happens naturally in our build or is a symptom of the register-pressure difference behind the residual.
frontier.mechanism: n/a until the .greg/.sched dump (frontier item 1) is read -- this is exactly the kind of allocation/scheduling question that dump answers directly rather than needing a guessed C lever.
frontier.next_probe: After reading the .greg/.sched dump for this function, check whether buf's address is already live across the whole loop in our RTL or gets recomputed; if recomputed, look for a C-level reason (e.g. an intervening statement that appears to clobber a0's preferred register).
